name: Tabs
summary: Panels of related content, one shown at a time, chosen from a row of tabs.

guidance.useFor: Related content in a few panels where people need one at a time: product details, specifications, reviews.
insteadUse: Content people should compare: show it together
Steps in order: a multi-step form
content: Keep panels independent: nothing in one should depend on another

rungReason: No native element: <lue-tabs> upgrades links to sections (which work without script) into the APG tabs pattern.

a11y.role: tablist, tab and tabpanel (written by the element)
a11y.name: The list's aria-label; each panel by its tab

keyboard.action: Next or previous tab, shown at once (wrapping; mirrored in right-to-left text)
From the selected tab into its panel
Show the focused tab (it already is: automatic activation)

focus.indicator: :focus-visible outline on the tab and the panel

elementRules: Links and panels need ids in the markup. The element finds tabs by .lue-tabs__list a[href^='#'] and panels by those ids; it fires lue-tab-change (detail.panel). React renders the no-script markup only.

props.label: the list's name
props.tabs: [{ id, label, content }]; the tab's id is `${id}-tab`

rules: The URL's #panel opens that tab first
To choose a value, use Segmented control: tabs switch content
The list is a <nav>: without script it's an in-page navigation landmark, and ARIA in HTML lets <nav> take role="tablist"
withoutJavaScript: A list of links to every section, all shown
contrast: A solid rule under the tabs
forcedColors: The selected tab has a Highlight bar
